The industrial surcharge program report is recommending lowering the total Keldell nitrogen
or TKN, limit in the sewer use bylaw from 100 milligrams a liter to 50 milligrams a liter,
and adding TKN to the industrial surcharge program beginning in January 2028.
We are bringing this forward to support regulatory compliance, protect the receiving environment,
and establish equitable cost recovery.
A ammonia concentrations entering the wastewater treatment plant have increased by approximately
65% over the past decade, and the water security agency has indicated that more stringent
year-round ammonia limits are forthcoming.
During winter, though we are meeting our permit to operate, we are exceeding environmental
quality objectives.
TKN is already listed as a restricted substance in our bylaw at 100 milligrams a liter, but it
has not included in our surcharge program.
As a result, we are not recovering the operating costs associated with removing it.
In 2024, the cost-removed TKN at the wastewater treatment plant was approximately $726,000, and
this cost is currently borne by all rate pairs.
We reviewed 13 Canadian municipalities, and all include TKN in their sewer use bylaws.
Eight currently included in their surcharge program, and three more are moving in that direction
now.
If approved, industries would have a two-year transition period before surcharge is take effect.
They can choose to invest in pre-treatment options to lower their TKN discharge, or choose
to pay the surcharge beginning in 2028.
Administration will continue refining the rate methodology, and will report back in 2027
with a final recommended surcharge rate.
This change alone will not achieve compliance with future permit limits.
Plant upgrades are still required.
However, this step helps us mitigate risk of non-compliance while ensuring treatment costs are
allocated fairly rather than borne by general rate pairs.
Should Council approve the recommendations?
The administration will begin engagement with industrial users this quarter.
